description: Extra inputs of AT-041e (trend, anomaly, official station type). Same format and checks as madrid_partitions.json; these terms are added to the AT-041d ones, they do not replace them. Terms are anchored on the measurement-uncertainty scale or on official metadata; nothing is estimated from data.

variables.rationale: no2_last - no2_lag3h: change of the finished hour [t-1h, t) with respect to the finished hour [t-4h, t-3h) (both known at t). Estable = |change| <= 6 ug/m3 (whole-number data). The half-width 6 ug/m3 is the measurement-uncertainty scale already used for the NO2 terms: 15 % of the first ICA breakpoint (40 ug/m3), i.e. the shoulder of the 'Buena' term (see madrid_partitions.json, no2_last). It says 'a change of more than the order of the measurement uncertainty', NOT a statistically significant change and NOT a physical threshold; the 15 % itself is an extrapolation of the data quality objective of Directive 2008/50/EC to low concentrations (see the caveats there). The shoulder is one more half-width (6 ug/m3), so the terms overlap smoothly.
variables.source_status: No external source for the use as a trend threshold; the 6 ug/m3 value is derived in madrid_partitions.json (Directive 2008/50/EC Annex I, read 2026-10-30 on legislation.gov.uk).

variables.rationale: no2_last minus the median of no2_last of the same station at the same local hour of the observed hour, computed on the TRAINING rows only (2019-2023, issue time before the training end). Normal = within 6 ug/m3 of that station-and-hour median. The half-width 6 ug/m3 is the measurement-uncertainty scale already used for the NO2 terms: 15 % of the first ICA breakpoint (40 ug/m3), i.e. the shoulder of the 'Buena' term (see madrid_partitions.json, no2_last). It says 'a change of more than the order of the measurement uncertainty', NOT a statistically significant change and NOT a physical threshold; the 15 % itself is an extrapolation of the data quality objective of Directive 2008/50/EC to low concentrations (see the caveats there). The shoulder is one more half-width (6 ug/m3), so the terms overlap smoothly. It is a difference to a typical value, not a z-score: on the training rows its interquartile range is 24 ug/m3 (quartiles -8 and +16) and 33 % of the rows fall in 'Normal' (|anomaly| <= 6), so 'Normal' is a narrow band.
variables.source_status: No external source; reference computed from the AT-012 table, training split only (leakage test in tests/ml/test_extra_features.py).

variables.rationale: Official station type from stations.geojson attribute station_type_code (Madrid geoportal layer 5: UT = Urbana trafico, UF = Urbana fondo, S = Suburbana), coded 0 / 1 / 2 only to feed the partition; the code has no order. Nothing is inferred: a station without a code raises. Whole-number input, so crisp.
variables.source_status: Official metadata of the Madrid air quality stations (geoportal layer already referenced by stations.geojson geometry_source); 24 stations: 9 UT, 12 UF, 3 S.
